# System-level simulation


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

System-level simulation in the sense of [Sionna
SYS](https://nvlabs.github.io/sionna/sys/index.html): what matters is
how many links work and how well, not the bits of each transmission. A
*PHY abstraction* replaces the bits. It maps a transmission’s SNR to a
packet error rate, and the packet is lost with that probability. It is
fast, so it suits training and large numbers of agents.
[`LinkLevelChannel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/link.html#linklevelchannel)
(see `link`) simulates the bits instead, and gives the same packet error
rates (tested there).

The decisions of the system also belong here, since they need no bits:
the transmit power and whether to transmit at all
([`PowerControl`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#powercontrol)).
Which links transmit when is decided by the
[`Protocol`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/protocol.html#protocol);
links that transmit at the same time interfere
([`InterferenceBackend`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#interferencebackend)).

[`RadioChannel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#radiochannel)
is what channels at both levels share. It computes the *link budget* of
a transmission: `h` from a
[`Fading`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/propagation.html#fading),
the power `P` from a
[`PowerControl`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#powercontrol),
and the SNR `P |h|² / noise_power`.

## PHY abstraction

A *PHY abstraction* gives the packet error rate of a transmission from
its SINR, without simulating its bits. An
[`ErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#errormodel)
does it for a batch of transmissions at once:

- [`BPSKErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#bpskerrormodel)
  (the default) uses uncoded BPSK over AWGN. Its bit error rate is
  `Q(√(2 SINR))`, with independent bit errors, so bigger packets fail
  more often.
- [`ThresholdErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#thresholderrormodel)
  receives a packet when the SINR is at or above a threshold.
- [`EESMErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#eesmerrormodel)
  combines the subcarriers by EESM, then applies a logistic packet-error
  curve with your calibration, e.g. a Wi-Fi MCS.
- [`SionnaErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/sionna_sys.html#sionnaerrormodel)
  (see `sionna_sys`) uses 5G NR with LDPC codes: Sionna SYS’s calibrated
  tables, the subcarriers combined by EESM, and link adaptation.

The two simple models use the mean SINR over the subcarriers. The
functions below are the analytic rates they use.

### eesm

``` python
def eesm(
    sinr:np.ndarray, # Linear SINR at each subcarrier
    beta:float, # EESM parameter (of an MCS)
)->float:
```

*Effective SINR (linear) of SINRs at several subcarriers: -β
ln(mean(exp(-SINR/β))).*

``` python
wifi = EESMErrorModel(beta=28.0, threshold_db=21.0, slope=1.5)              # ~802.11ac MCS 7 (approximate)
per, _, info = wifi([np.full(52, 10 ** 2.1), np.full(52, 10 ** 2.6)], np.array([8000, 8000]))
assert abs(per[0] - 0.1) < 1e-9 and per[1] < 0.01 and abs(info[0]['sinr_eff_db'] - 21) < 1e-9   # 10% at the threshold
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
faded = 10 ** 2.1 * np.abs((rng.standard_normal(52) + 1j * rng.standard_normal(52)) / np.sqrt(2)) ** 2
assert eesm(faded, 28.0) < np.mean(faded)                                   # faded subcarriers count for more
assert wifi([np.zeros(52)], np.array([100]))[0][0] == 1.0
assert wifi([np.full(52, 10 ** 2.1)], np.array([16000]))[0][0] > per[0]     # bigger packets fail more
```

``` python
per, symbols, _ = BPSKErrorModel()([np.array([10 ** 0.6]), np.array([10 ** 0.2, 10.0])], np.array([100, 100]))
assert np.allclose(per, [packet_error_rate(6, 100), packet_error_rate(10 * np.log10((10 ** 0.2 + 10) / 2), 100)])
assert symbols.tolist() == [100, 100]
assert ThresholdErrorModel(10)([np.array([9.9]), np.array([10.0])], np.array([8, 8]))[0].tolist() == [1.0, 0.0]
```

## Power control

A
[`PowerControl`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#powercontrol)
decides the transmit power `P` from the channel gain `|h|²`, and whether
to transmit at all. A link it does not use is an *outage*: nothing is
sent, so the receiver gets nothing.

- [`FixedPower`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#fixedpower)
  uses the same power always, by default the link’s `tx_power_w`.
- [`ChannelInversion`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#channelinversion)
  uses just enough power to reach a target SNR: `P = γ σ² / |h|²`, where
  `γ` is the target SNR and `σ²` the noise power. A link needing more
  than `max_power` is not used.
- [`MessagePower`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#messagepower)
  uses the power the sender chose, e.g. a learned power control, put in
  the message’s metadata.

`allocate` is vectorized (numpy arrays or torch tensors), so training
code can handle a whole batch of links at once.

href="https://github.com/Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh/comm-core/blob/main/comm_core/system.py#L192"

## Radio channels

The link budget of a transmission, and what both levels share: a
[`Fading`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/propagation.html#fading),
a
[`PowerControl`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#powercontrol),
the noise power and a random generator. Subclasses decide what arrives.

**The results** of both levels report the SNR, the energy (power ×
duration) and the latency (symbols / bandwidth, 0 with an infinite
bandwidth). Their `metadata` holds `channel_gain_db` and `tx_power`, and
`outage` for links the power control did not use (`success=False`, 0
bits sent).

A transmission can be given the power of other transmissions at its
receiver (`interference`, see
[`InterferenceBackend`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#interferencebackend)).
Its `snr_db` is then the SINR, `P |h|² / (noise_power + interference)`,
and the metadata has `interference_power`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh/comm-core/blob/main/comm_core/system.py#L229"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## System-level channel

A transmission’s SINR gives its packet error rate (the
[`ErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#errormodel)),
and the packet is lost with that probability. A packet that arrives is
the payload as sent.

- **Size and timing:** `message.size_bits` is the packet size. The
  timing counts the symbols the error model reports: one per bit for the
  simple models, the resource elements for
  [`SionnaErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/sionna_sys.html#sionnaerrormodel).
- **Batches:** `transmit_batch` handles several transmissions with one
  call of the error model. The backends use it for a step’s
  transmissions.
- **Subcarriers:** with a frequency-selective fading
  (e.g. [`RayTracedPathsFading`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/propagation.html#raytracedpathsfading)
  with subcarriers), the error model gets the SINR at each subcarrier.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh/comm-core/blob/main/comm_core/system.py#L313"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### SystemLevelChannel

``` python
def SystemLevelChannel(
    fading:Fading | None=None, # The coefficient h of a transmission; None: h = 1
    power_control:PowerControl | None=None, # Transmit power and outages; None: the link's tx_power_w
    noise_power:float=1.0, # Noise power at the receiver
    per_model:str | ErrorModel='bpsk', # 'bpsk', 'threshold', or an `ErrorModel` (e.g. `SionnaErrorModel`)
    snr_threshold_db:float=10.0, # The 'threshold' model's SNR
    seed:int | None=None, # Seed of the packet losses and the fading
):
```

*A PHY abstraction: SINR -\> packet error rate -\> the packet arrives
intact or is lost. No bits are simulated.*

### Tests

``` python
def send(ch, link=Link('a', 'b'), n=1, size_bits=100, **metadata):
    t = Transmission(message=Message('a', 'b', 'hi', size_bits=size_bits, metadata=metadata), sender='a', receiver='b', start_time=0.0)
    return [ch.transmit(t, link) for _ in range(n)]

for snr_db, delivered in ((10, 1.0), (0, 0.0)):                 # 100 bits: always through at 10 dB, never at 0 dB
    rs = send(SystemLevelChannel(noise_power=10 ** (-snr_db / 10), seed=0), n=50)
    assert np.mean([r.success for r in rs]) == delivered and abs(rs[0].snr_db - snr_db) < 1e-9
r = rs[0]
assert r.size_bits == 100 and r.energy == 100 and r.latency == 0 and r.metadata == {'channel_gain_db': 0.0, 'tx_power': 1.0}
# in between: lost as often as the packet error rate says, reproducibly
ch = SystemLevelChannel(noise_power=10 ** -0.6, seed=0)        # 6 dB, 100 bits
ch.reset(seed=3); first = [r.success for r in send(ch, n=2000)]
ch.reset(seed=3); assert [r.success for r in send(ch, n=2000)] == first
assert abs(1 - np.mean(first) - packet_error_rate(6, 100)) < 0.03
# the threshold model, channel inversion (outages), a perfect link, a finite bandwidth
assert send(SystemLevelChannel(noise_power=1.0, per_model='threshold', snr_threshold_db=-1))[0].success
for h, sent in ((1.2, True), (0.1, False)):
    r, = send(SystemLevelChannel(fading=NoFading(h), power_control=ChannelInversion(10, max_power=10)))
    assert r.success == sent and r.size_bits == (100 if sent else 0) and r.metadata.get('outage', False) != sent
r, = send(SystemLevelChannel(fading=NoFading(math.inf), noise_power=1e9))
assert r.success and r.snr_db == math.inf
r, = send(SystemLevelChannel(), link=Link('a', 'b', bandwidth_hz=1e6, tx_power_w=0.5))
assert abs(r.latency - 1e-4) < 1e-15 and abs(r.energy - 0.5e-4) < 1e-15
```

``` python
# a frequency-selective fading: the error model gets the SINR at each subcarrier
class TwoSubcarriers(Fading):
    def coefficient(self, transmission, link):
        return 1.0
    def response(self, transmission, link):
        return np.array([1.0, 0.1])                                      # the second subcarrier faded by 20 dB

class Recorder(ErrorModel):
    def __call__(self, sinr, size_bits):
        self.sinr = sinr
        return np.zeros(len(sinr)), np.asarray(size_bits), [{'seen': True} for _ in sinr]

recorder = Recorder()
r, = send(SystemLevelChannel(fading=TwoSubcarriers(), noise_power=0.1, per_model=recorder))
assert np.allclose(recorder.sinr[0], [10.0, 0.1]) and r.metadata['seen']
assert abs(r.snr_db - 10 * np.log10(np.mean([10.0, 0.1]))) < 1e-9          # the mean SNR
# a batch: the same results as one at a time, with one call of the error model
ch1, ch2 = SystemLevelChannel(noise_power=10 ** -0.6, seed=4), SystemLevelChannel(noise_power=10 ** -0.6, seed=4)
pairs = [(Transmission(message=Message('a', 'b', k, size_bits=100), sender='a', receiver='b', start_time=0.0), Link('a', 'b')) for k in range(50)]
assert [r.success for r in ch1.transmit_batch(pairs)] == [ch2.transmit(t, l).success for t, l in pairs]
try:
    SystemLevelChannel(per_model='qam'); raise AssertionError('no error')
except ValueError:
    pass
```

In a
[`Network`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/network.html#network),
the topology and the protocol decide which transmissions happen, and the
channel decides what arrives:

``` python
from comm_core import Network, Node, FullMeshTopology, IdealProtocol, AnalyticalBackend
from comm_core.propagation import RayleighFading
```

``` python
ch = SystemLevelChannel(fading=RayleighFading(), power_control=ChannelInversion(10, max_power=20), seed=0)
nodes = ['a', 'b', 'c']
net = Network([Node(n) for n in nodes], FullMeshTopology(nodes), IdealProtocol(), AnalyticalBackend(ch))
net.reset(seed=0)
for step in range(20):
    for s in nodes:
        for r in nodes:
            if s != r:
                net.send(Message(s, r, payload=step, size_bits=64))
    net.step()
m = net.metrics.summary()
assert m.transmissions == 20 * 6 and 0 < m.failed < m.transmissions        # deep fades: outages
```

## Interference

[`InterferenceBackend`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#interferencebackend)
makes the transmissions of a
[`Network`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/network.html#network)
step share one medium: they happen at the same time and interfere. Each
transmission’s SINR counts the power the other senders put at its
receiver,

`SINR = P |h|² / (noise_power + Σ P' |h'|²)`,

where `P'` is another sender’s power and `h'` the coefficient from it to
the receiver, from the same fading. The interference is treated as
Gaussian noise. Then:

- **Half-duplex** (the default): a node that transmits in a step cannot
  receive in it.
- **One radio per node**: a sender’s transmissions in a step don’t
  interfere with each other, and it interferes with others at its
  strongest transmit power.
- **Power control** is open-loop:
  [`ChannelInversion`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#channelinversion)
  targets the SNR, not the SINR.

It works with both levels:
[`SystemLevelChannel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#systemlevelchannel)
uses the SINR for the packet error rate, and
[`LinkLevelChannel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/link.html#linklevelchannel)
adds the interference to the noise of every bit.

Whether to avoid simultaneous transmissions is the
[`Protocol`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/protocol.html#protocol)’s
job:
[`TDMAProtocol`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/protocol.html#tdmaprotocol)
gives each node its own slots, and
[`SlottedALOHA`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/protocol.html#slottedaloha)
transmits at random (see `protocol`). With
[`IdealProtocol`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/protocol.html#idealprotocol),
everything sent before a step goes out in that step, so if every node
talks at once, nobody hears (half-duplex).

<a
href="https://github.com/Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh/comm-core/blob/main/comm_core/system.py#L389"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### InterferenceBackend.transmit_all

``` python
def transmit_all(
    transmissions:List[Tuple[Transmission, Link]], # The transmissions of one step, with their links
)->List[TransmissionResult]:
```

*The transmissions of one step, at the same time.*

### Tests

``` python
from comm_core.propagation import RayTracedFading
```

``` python
# 21 positions on a line, |H|^2 = 1e-6 / d^3 (d in cells)
xs = np.arange(21)
d = np.abs(np.subtract.outer(xs, xs)).astype(float)
H = np.where(d > 0, 1e-3 / np.maximum(d, 1) ** 1.5, 0)
table = RayTracedFading(H, [(x, 0) for x in xs])
ch = SystemLevelChannel(fading=table, noise_power=1e-10, per_model='threshold', snr_threshold_db=10, seed=0)
backend = InterferenceBackend(ch)
def tx(s, r, bits=64):
    return Transmission(message=Message(s, r, 'hi', size_bits=bits), sender=s, receiver=r, start_time=0.0), Link(s, r)

table.set_positions({'a': (0, 0), 'b': (1, 0), 'c': (20, 0), 'd': (19, 0)})
alone, = backend.transmit_all([tx('a', 'b')])
assert alone.success and abs(alone.snr_db - 40) < 1e-9                 # 1 W x 1e-6 / 1e-10: 40 dB
# c -> d far away: a little interference at b
far = backend.transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('c', 'd')])
i = 1e-6 / 19 ** 3
assert all(r.success for r in far) and abs(far[0].metadata['interference_power'] - i) < 1e-20
assert abs(far[0].snr_db - 10 * np.log10(1e-6 / (1e-10 + i))) < 1e-9
# c -> d next to b: a-b drops to 9 dB, below the threshold; c-d (a is 4 cells from d) still gets through
table.set_positions({'c': (3, 0), 'd': (4, 0)})
near = backend.transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('c', 'd')])
assert not near[0].success and 8.9 < near[0].snr_db < 9.1 and near[1].success
# half-duplex: a and b talk to each other at once, neither hears
both = backend.transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('b', 'a')])
assert not any(r.success for r in both) and all(r.metadata['half_duplex'] for r in both) and both[0].size_bits == 64
assert all(r.success for r in InterferenceBackend(ch, half_duplex=False).transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('b', 'a')]))
# one sender, two receivers: no interference with itself
two = backend.transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('a', 'c')])
assert all(r.success for r in two) and 'interference_power' not in two[0].metadata
# outages are not on the air: they don't interfere
ch_inv = SystemLevelChannel(fading=table, power_control=ChannelInversion(20, max_power=1e-6), noise_power=1e-10)
r = InterferenceBackend(ch_inv).transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('c', 'd')])
assert all(x.metadata.get('outage') for x in r)                        # each needs 1e-2 W > 1e-6 W
```

In a
[`Network`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/network.html#network),
a step’s transmissions are the ones that happen at the same time:

``` python
from comm_core import Network, Node, FullMeshTopology, IdealProtocol
```

``` python
nodes = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']
net = Network([Node(n) for n in nodes], FullMeshTopology(nodes), IdealProtocol(), InterferenceBackend(ch))
table.set_positions({'a': (0, 0), 'b': (1, 0), 'c': (20, 0), 'd': (19, 0)})
net.send(Message('a', 'b', 'x', size_bits=64))
net.send(Message('c', 'd', 'y', size_bits=64))
assert [r.success for r in net.step()] == [True, True] and net.receive('b')[0].payload == 'x'
# everybody talks at once: every node is transmitting, so nobody hears
for s in nodes:
    for r in nodes:
        if s != r:
            net.send(Message(s, r, 'z', size_bits=64))
assert not any(r.success for r in net.step())
```
